Blasting through dungeons without ever having to pause, killing entities called "death lords" with one or two blows, and no monsters harder than them... it's fun for the first two dungeons, after that the only fun is in collecting loot.

I don't think "too easy" and "too hard" apply really. That's what difficulty settings are for. The real genius in a well-designed game is keeping the player challenged about the same all the way through, and giving him things that are difficult but possible. Make it so on "easy" the player has it just as easy on the first level as the tenth. The same for "hard".
I want a game to be interesting. I don't find reloading and replaying the same segment over and over very interesting.

Imho, "easy modo" does allow you to get through the game faster, but also kills any sense of achievement you may get from playing it.

To illustrate: I recently did a re-run of Postal 2 in Postal Mode. Shits brutal, and it could be quite frustrating at times, but nothing beats the feeling of utter satisfaction when you eventually power through it. Same reason with the popularity of the Dark Souls series.

Sometimes, the true joy of playing a game comes from you knowing that you actually got gud enough to beat it.

No matter how many times you play a level, it doesn't change. The enemies are in the same places, the power ups too. If you just pay attention and learn what to do, you'll be fine. It's not that hard. And the levels aren't even that long either. You'll be fine.

Same thing applied to games like Doom. Then something weird happened to FPS games. The levels began getting much, much longer. I might beat a level of Doom in 3 minutes. Getting to the next checkpoint in Wolfenstein: The New Order could take a while. Especially when you end up in one of those shooting galleries with wave after wave of enemies. And a single level, of which there are only 9 or 10, is like an hour each! And then you have games like Borderlands which have respawning, but all this laborious boring travel to get back to where you were. Or worse, since RPG mechanics are worked into everything now, maybe you'll die and feel like you lost precious "progress" of your numbers becoming bigger numbers.

Eventually, incrementally, your numbers will beat their numbers and you'll progress.
